# Cohub

> A living space where people and agents create, play, and build together.

Cohub is open source (Apache-2.0) and self-hostable. A Space is a cloud workspace with files, a sandbox, Saves (checkpoints) and published Apps; people and agents work in it together, from the web, the CLI or chat apps.

## Docs

- [Overview](https://cohub.live/docs): Cohub is a living Space where people and agents create, save, share, and build from real context.
- [Core concepts](https://cohub.live/docs/learn/core-concepts): The objects that make up Cohub — Space, Chat, Save, Sandbox, App, and more.
- [Product map](https://cohub.live/docs/learn/product-map): A compact map of the Cohub UI — sidebar, Chat, preview, and settings.
- [Quick start](https://cohub.live/docs/learn/quick-start): Create a Space, chat with an Agent, touch files, save a checkpoint, and publish an App.
- [Spaces](https://cohub.live/docs/workspace/spaces): Create, open, configure, and think with Spaces as the main unit of work in Cohub.
- [Chats](https://cohub.live/docs/workspace/chats): Use Chats and the composer to work with Agents — models, turns, forks, skills, and sharing.
- [Files & Sandbox](https://cohub.live/docs/workspace/files-and-sandbox): Use the Space workspace, Sandbox runtime, ports, and previews as the durable project surface.
- [Saves](https://cohub.live/docs/workspace/saves): Capture immutable Space checkpoints, review diffs, restore, and build from known-good states.
- [Apps](https://cohub.live/docs/create/apps): Publish a Space file, directory, or port as a shareable Cohub App with versions and permissions.
- [App development](https://cohub.live/docs/developers/apps): Build a Cohub App — runtime context, permissions, prompts, generation, files, actions, surfaces, and commerce.
- [CLI](https://cohub.live/docs/developers/cli): Install Cohub CLI, sign in, and run the main Space workflows from your terminal.
- [SDK](https://cohub.live/docs/developers/sdk): Use the Cohub TypeScript SDK for Spaces, Chats, Apps, realtime updates, and App runtime APIs.

## Use cases

- [Cohub use cases: who uses a Space, and for what](https://cohub.live/use-cases): Each page names who it is for, the moment they reach for Cohub, and why a Space fits. Every claim links to its source.
- [AI agent in Discord, WeChat, Telegram and Feishu | Cohub](https://cohub.live/use-cases/agent-in-discord-wechat): To run an AI agent in Discord, WeChat, Telegram, Feishu or QQ, bind the messenger to a Cohub Space as a Channel; messages go to the Space's agent and replies come back in the same chat.
- [AI research workspace with shared context across Spaces](https://cohub.live/use-cases/ai-research-workspace): Cohub works as an AI research workspace with shared context: keep each source collection in its own Space, then @mention it for one question or mount it read-only so every Chat can read it.
- [AI agent workspace for indie developers | Cohub](https://cohub.live/use-cases/indie-developer-ai-workspace): Cohub is an AI agent workspace for indie developers: each Space has a cloud sandbox the agent runs commands in, port previews, one-command publishing and prompts that run on a schedule.
- [Multiplayer AI chat: build with friends and an agent](https://cohub.live/use-cases/multiplayer-ai-chat): Cohub turns a multiplayer AI chat into a shared project: friends join one Space, talk to the same agent, see each other's Chats and files, and publish the result as an App.
- [Publish a running app from an AI sandbox with Cohub](https://cohub.live/use-cases/publish-app-from-ai-sandbox): To publish a running app from an AI sandbox in Cohub, point an App at the port your dev server listens on; static output can go out as a folder or a single HTML file instead.
- [Schedule AI agent tasks that run in your workspace](https://cohub.live/use-cases/schedule-ai-agent-tasks): You schedule AI agent tasks in Cohub with a scheduled prompt: a message the Space sends to its agent once at a set time or on a cron schedule, with every run kept as a Chat.
- [Self-hosted AI workspace with agents and sandboxes | Cohub](https://cohub.live/use-cases/self-hosted-ai-workspace): Cohub can run as a self-hosted AI workspace: deploy the Apache-2.0 source on your Kubernetes cluster, sign in through your OIDC provider, and point the agent at your own model keys.
- [Shared AI context for teams: one Space, every Chat visible](https://cohub.live/use-cases/team-shared-ai-context): Cohub provides shared AI context for teams: Chats in a Space are visible to its members, the agent works on the same files for everyone, and anyone can continue or fork a teammate's thread.

## Compare

- [Cohub compared: alternatives and when to choose each](https://cohub.live/compare): Side by side with the tools people already use. Each page says what the other product does better and when to choose it, citing its official docs.
- [ChatGPT Projects alternative with a real computer: Cohub](https://cohub.live/compare/chatgpt-projects-alternative): Looking for a ChatGPT Projects alternative? Cohub keeps chats, files and instructions together like a Project, and each Space also has a sandbox the agent runs commands in, publishable Apps and scheduled prompts.
- [Claude Projects alternative for shared, running work: Cohub](https://cohub.live/compare/claude-projects-alternative): As a Claude Projects alternative, Cohub keeps chats, files and instructions in a Space like a Project, and adds a sandbox the agent runs code in, @mentions of other Spaces, and Apps you can publish.
- [Cursor cloud agents alternative for shared Spaces: Cohub](https://cohub.live/compare/cursor-alternative): Cohub is a Cursor cloud agents alternative when the job ends in a running App rather than a pull request: a shared Space with a sandbox, published Apps, schedules and chat-app access, open source.
- [Open source Devin alternative you can self-host: Cohub](https://cohub.live/compare/devin-alternative): If you need an open source Devin alternative, Cohub is Apache-2.0 and self-hostable: agents work in per-Space sandboxes, run on schedules or events, and publish Apps, with your own model keys.
- [Notion AI alternative for teams that build: Cohub](https://cohub.live/compare/notion-ai-alternative): Cohub is a Notion AI alternative for teams whose AI work ends in running software or automations: a shared Space where the agent edits files, runs code in a sandbox and publishes Apps.
- [Replit Agent alternative for building together: Cohub](https://cohub.live/compare/replit-agent-alternative): Cohub is a Replit Agent alternative for building in a shared Space: an agent with its own sandbox, Chats every member can see and continue, Apps published from a file, folder or port, and an open-source core.

## Features

- [Cohub features: context network, schedules and hooks](https://cohub.live/features): When to reach for each of these three, and which one fits. Commands and settings live in the docs, linked from every page.
- [Context network: share context between AI workspaces](https://cohub.live/features/context-network): Cohub's context network is how you share context between AI workspaces: @mention a Space for one message, mount it as a read-only Mod, fork a Save into a new Space, or hand work to another Space.
- [Scheduled prompts: cron for AI agents in Cohub](https://cohub.live/features/scheduled-prompts): Scheduled prompts are cron for AI agents: a Cohub prompt sent to a Space after a delay, at an ISO time, or on a cron expression with a time zone, with each run recorded in a Chat.
- [Space hooks: run scripts on AI agent events in Cohub](https://cohub.live/features/space-hooks): Space hooks let you run scripts on AI agent events in Cohub: a YAML file in .cohub/hooks/ runs a command, sends a prompt or calls an App Action when a turn finishes, files change, a Save is created or a webhook arrives.

## Guides

- [Cohub guides: step by step to a finished result](https://cohub.live/guides): Each guide walks to one finished result. Reference material stays in the docs.
- [Self-host an AI agent platform: deploy Cohub step by step](https://cohub.live/guides/self-host-cohub): To self-host an AI agent platform with Cohub, provision Kubernetes, Postgres, Redis, shared storage, S3-compatible object storage and an OIDC provider, then deploy each service from the repository's templates.
